method.protocol: 0 K static relaxation (BFGS, fmax 0.01 eV/A). Cu(111) p(3x3) 4-layer slab, 8 A vacuum each side, bottom 2 layers fixed, MACE-relaxed a0=3.640 A. O started at fcc/hcp/top/bridge; fcc lowest (bridge relaxes into fcc). E_ads = E(slab+O) - E(slab) - E(O atom), O atom = single O in a 20 A box (the model's isolated-atom energy, -1.548 eV)

payload.note: Most stable site is the fcc hollow. E_ads = -4.84 eV at 1/9 ML (p(3x3)), -4.90 eV at 1/4 ML (p(2x2)). Going from 4 to 6 layers changes it by <0.003 eV. hcp is 0.05-0.07 eV weaker, ontop ~1.75 eV weaker. Referenced to 1/2 O2 (MACE): -1.70 eV (1/9 ML) / -1.76 eV (1/4 ML). VALIDATION against independent known results using the same model and setup: Cu a0 3.640 A (exp 3.615 A; PBE is typically ~3.63 A); Cu cohesive energy vs the model's own isolated-atom energy 3.50 eV (exp ~3.49 eV); O2 bond length 1.235 A; O2 binding energy vs the model's own O-atom energy 6.29 eV, close to the PBE value (~6.2 eV, PBE 1996 paper; exp ~5.2 eV). That last check matters most: it shows the model's isolated-O energy acts like a PBE-quality gas-phase atom reference, so the result is effectively a PBE-level number. UNCERTAINTY (+/-0.4 eV) covers: (i) the exchange-correlation functional and atom reference, the dominant term. PBE overbinds the O atom relative to O2 by ~0.5 eV per O2. Combining the computed 1/2 O2 adsorption energy with the experimental O2 binding energy (De ~5.21 eV) gives about -4.30 eV instead of -4.84 eV. (ii) Published DFT values for O at Cu(111) hollows referenced to atomic O range from about -4.3 eV (Xu & Mavrikakis, Surf. Sci. 494, 131 (2001), PW91) to about -5.0 eV (fcc, a more recent DFT study). (iii) Coverage dependence ~0.07 eV. (iv) MLIP error vs DFT ~0.1 eV, estimated not measured. No experimental adsorption energy referenced to atomic O was found in /data/calibration/tier1.json. No zero-point or thermal corrections are included.

_fulfilled_need.query: Compute the adsorption energy of atomic oxygen on Cu(111) at its most stable site, referenced to an isolated O atom.
